issues.description: Register chosen to hold the pixel value for printing differs between artifacts. The problem statement explicitly instructs that the pixel value read from memory should be loaded into ECX ("mov ecx, [esi]") so it is available for the subsequent printf sequence (problem_statement.md lines 24-27). The template's printf call pushes ECX as the first printf argument (template_repository/pixel.asm lines 112-118). The solution, however, loads the pixel value into EAX ("mov eax, [esi]") at solution_repository/pixel.asm line 101, leaving ECX unchanged when the template-style printf push sequence executes. This mismatch means the value printed (from ECX) will not be the memory pixel value in the solution, which will confuse students trying to map the textual instruction and template call order to the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make register usage consistent between problem statement, template, and solution. Preferred fixes: (A) Change the solution to load the memory pixel into ECX (replace "mov eax, [esi]" with "mov ecx, [esi]") so the existing printf push order (push ecx; push ebx; push eax; push message) prints the correct value; or (B) if retaining the solution's use of EAX is desired, update the template's printf push ordering and the problem text to expect EAX (adjust pushes to push eax; push ebx; push eax_or_other as needed) and update the instruction in the problem statement to reference EAX. Ensure any register save/restore sequences preserve the chosen register across the printf call.
